source: Kumar and Clark Clinical Medicine 11th Ed 2025
chapter: Chapter 24: Biliary tract and pancreatic disease

1_pathophysiology.definition: Adenomyomatosis is a gall bladder abnormality characterized by hyperplasia of the mucosa, thickening of the muscle wall, and multiple intramural diverticula (the so-called 'Rokitansky-Aschoff sinuses').
1_pathophysiology.mechanism: The condition has been suggested to be secondary to increased intraluminal gall bladder pressure but this is not proven. The hyperplastic changes involve both the mucosal layer and the muscularis propria, with formation of diverticula within the wall.
1_pathophysiology.classification: Can occur in different distributions: (1) Diffuse adenomyomatosis; (2) Segmental distribution -- particularly associated with coexisting gallstones; (3) Fundal form. The segmental form is more likely to have coexisting gallstones, but there is no evidence to support a direct relationship between the two.

modifiable: Diet high in animal fat/low in fibre
Obesity with or without metabolic syndrome
Rapid weight loss (e.g., very low-calorie diet)
non_modifiable: Sex (rates are equal in males and females, unlike cholelithiasis which is F > M)

epidemiology.age_group: Not specifically stated; detected as incidental finding during investigation for possible gallstone disease
epidemiology.sex_predominance: Rates are equal in males and females (in contrast to cholelithiasis)

cardinal_symptoms: Unlikely that adenomyomatosis alone is a cause of biliary symptoms

inspection: Incidental finding during investigation for possible gallstone disease
palpation: Right upper quadrant tenderness (may be present but not specific)
percussion: Focal tenderness over gall bladder region
auscultation: Reduced or absent bowel sounds in severe disease

atypical_presentations: Asymptomatic -- most commonly an incidental finding
May coexist with gallstones without causing additional symptoms
Segmental distribution form may have more prominent features due to associated gallstones

4_laboratory_investigations.expected_finding: May be marginally elevated in the presence of cholecystitis alone
4_laboratory_investigations.clinical_significance: Helps identify associated bile duct obstruction and differentiate from other causes of right upper quadrant pain

4_laboratory_investigations.expected_finding: May show moderate leucocytosis if acute exacerbation present
4_laboratory_investigations.clinical_significance: Supports diagnosis of cholecystitis; helps assess severity of sepsis

4_laboratory_investigations.expected_finding: May be raised if acute exacerbation present
4_laboratory_investigations.clinical_significance: Useful for assessing disease severity and prognosis

5_radiological_investigations.expected_finding: Evidence of diseased gall bladder wall; thickening of the muscle wall
5_radiological_investigations.clinical_significance: Used to guide decision for cholecystectomy in the absence of defined gall bladder stones. Identifies gall bladder wall abnormalities and inflammatory changes.

5_radiological_investigations.expected_finding: Gall bladder wall thickening; intramural diverticula
5_radiological_investigations.clinical_significance: Used to define pathology when clinical situation fails to respond to conservative management.

5_radiological_investigations.expected_finding: Hyperplasia of the mucosa, thickening of the muscle wall, and multiple intramural diverticula (Rokitansky-Aschoff sinuses)

6_differential_diagnosis.distinguishing_feature: Most patients with chronic right hypochondrial pain are suffering from functional bowel disease rather than true gall bladder pathology

6_differential_diagnosis.condition: Irritable bowel syndrome (spasm of hepatic flexure)
6_differential_diagnosis.distinguishing_feature: Hepatic flexure syndrome mimics biliary colic; pain may be identical to original gallstone pain
Polypoid cholesterolosis and adenomyomatosis may mimic adenomatous polyps; only reliable predictor of malignant risk is polyp size (>10 mm)

6_differential_diagnosis.condition: Carcinoma of the right side of colon
6_differential_diagnosis.distinguishing_feature: May present with similar right upper quadrant pain and jaundice
Epigastric pain may mimic biliary colic; responds to acid suppression
Pain radiates differently (to groin rather than shoulder); associated with urinary symptoms

7_diagnostic_criteria.criteria_name: Clinical diagnosis guided by history and imaging findings, confirmed histologically
7_diagnostic_criteria.scoring_system: Clinical diagnosis -- no specific scoring system; diagnosis is primarily clinical, guided by imaging findings and confirmed histologically
criteria_list: Incidental finding during investigation for possible gallstone disease
Evidence of diseased gall bladder wall on ultrasound scanning
Hyperplasia of the mucosa with thickening of the muscle wall
Multiple intramural diverticula (Rokitansky-Aschoff sinuses) on histopathology

8_complications.complication: Coexistence with gallstones (frequently coexist, particularly in segmental distribution)

primary_prevention: Maintain healthy weight and avoid obesity/metabolic syndrome
Avoid rapid weight loss (which increases risk of cholesterol gallstones)
Dietary modifications: high in fibre, low in animal fat/cholesterol
secondary_prevention: Cholecystectomy when clinically indicated for symptomatic disease
9_prevention.screening: Not routinely recommended; diagnosis guided by clinical features and ultrasound findings

lifestyle_modifications: Weight management (avoid obesity and rapid weight loss)
Smoking cessation (independent risk factor for chronic pancreatitis and pancreatic cancer)
dietary_changes: Avoid high-fat meals which may precipitate biliary colic
10_non_pharmacological_treatment.physical_activity: Early mobilization after cholecystectomy (short period of ileus)
other: Cholecystectomy when clinically indicated for symptomatic disease

first_line.duration: Long-term therapy required; high recurrence rate when stopped
first_line.notes: Solubilizes pure or near-pure cholesterol stones by increasing bile salt content of bile
Reduce cholesterol secretion into bile; promote gallstone dissolution

second_line.notes: Suppresses uptake of dietary and biliary cholesterol across enterocyte brush border membrane

drugs_to_avoid.notes: Theoretical risk of exacerbating pancreatic ductal hypertension via sphincter of Oddi contraction; may worsen biliary/pancreatic pain

12_interventional_treatment.indication: Treatment of choice for virtually all patients with symptomatic gall bladder stones; day-care procedure in elective setting
12_interventional_treatment.timing: Elective (minimize waiting time to avoid 30% recurrent symptoms over 4 months); during admission if specific complications present
12_interventional_treatment.notes: Replaced laparotomy approach. Mortality 0.2%. Complications: biliary leak, bile duct injury (up to 0.5%), especially with variant duct anatomy

12_interventional_treatment.indication: Reserved for small proportion of patients with contraindications to laparoscopic approach
12_interventional_treatment.timing: Elective or urgent depending on clinical situation
12_interventional_treatment.notes: Contraindications: extensive previous upper abdominal surgery, ongoing bile duct obstruction, portal hypertension. 5% of laparoscopic cases converted
